summary: @servicetitan/eslint-plugin preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727KB payload
details: The package declares a `preinstall` hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads a Bun runtime archive from GitHub, extracts it, and then invokes `bun math_init.js` against a sibling file bundled inside the tarball. `math_init.js` is a 727KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (string-array rotator `WV8StW`, hex-numbered identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, sha256 9fc2570b7cef51c1b8df116d144d11ff4096357be7d2c4c6367cfc2509cf1bcc) that is not referenced by the plugin's `dist/index.js` and has no ESLint-rule purpose. `setup.mjs` itself is obfuscated with the same style (hex identifiers `_0x488df8`/`_0x52943e`, string-map indirection `_0x19328d.YCZJE(...)`), and includes a Linux-libc-detection branch that shells out to `ldd --version` and reads `/etc/os-release` to select an Alpine/musl-matched Bun build. The Bun runtime is fetched specifically so the payload executes outside Node's reachability, bypassing Node-based install-time analysis. The plugin name and scope impersonate a legitimate `@servicetitan` developer tool. Installing the package causes attacker-controlled code shipped in `math_init.js` to run on the installer's machine at `npm install` time under a runtime the package itself fetches and drops.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
